artifacts.summary: Full 6-phase implementation summary: qualified the verification-tier tie-break across all four planning surfaces plus one incidental label fix, with the plan itself executing as its own acceptance demonstration; final gate 33/35 green with 2 reasoned exclusions (both root-caused to a pre-existing, unrelated runtime-file-detection gap).

completion_data.completion_summary: Qualified plan-format.md's verification-tier tie-break from an unconditional strictest-tier default to a cost-aware rule requiring a **Tier Justification** field on every non-final phase, propagated identically to planner-agent.md, task-breakdown.md, and phase-closure.md, and fixed one stale label in plan-format-enforcement.md. The plan executed as its own acceptance demonstration: 5 non-final phases declared tiers below full with stated justifications, and the final phase ran the complete gate set (33/35 green; 2 findings closed as reasoned exclusions, both traced to a pre-existing, unrelated per-session runtime-file-detection gap unconnected to any of the five edited files).

memory_candidates.content: Tactic for mapping a touched path to its covering test suite(s) before writing a verification-tier justification in this agent system: source scripts/lib/suite-selection-lib.sh and call suite_selection_select("<repo-relative-path>"). It returns either a newline-separated list of covering suite basenames (feed to run-all.sh --only) or the sentinel __FULL_SWEEP__ meaning no suite maps to that path at all (common for pure-guidance markdown: agent-definition files, workflow/contract docs). In the __FULL_SWEEP__ case, the honest cheap-tier covering check is a gate subset of verify-deploy.sh (--only-gate 3,4 for doc-lint + task-reference-lint), never a suite subset -- claiming suite coverage that doesn't exist, or falling back to full by default, are the two failure modes a cost-aware tier-selection rule has to explicitly guard against.

hooks/detect-noop-bash.sh writes a per-session runtime state file at tmp/noop-bash-shapes-<session-uuid> on every Bash-tool call (detect-noop-bash.sh:251), a sibling mechanism to the already-documented tmp/noop-bash-count-* exclusion class in context/patterns/deploy-orphan-detection.md -- but the -shapes- filename isn't yet listed in that exclusion table. On a repo with multiple concurrently-dispatched agent sessions, verify-deploy.sh's gate 13 (whole-tree orphan detection) will reliably flag these as orphans, and any test fixture that symlinks (not copies) the live .claude/ tree -- e.g. test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh's baseline sanity check -- inherits the same finding and fails for a reason unrelated to its own subject. When diagnosing an unexplained gate-8/gate-13 failure during a concurrent multi-agent orchestration cycle, check for tmp/noop-bash-shapes-* and tmp/noop-bash-count-* before assuming a real regression.
